paper.title: Minimax-Optimal Online Contract Design with Unrestricted Bounded Contracts

settings.name_in_paper: Online contract design with unrestricted bounded contracts and outcome-category feedback
unmapped: Principal-agent contract design: principal posts payment vector f in [0,1]^m over m outcomes; a fresh agent type drawn i.i.d. selects a best response (fixed selection rule under ties); principal's utility P(f)·(v-f) may be discontinuous in f
Feedback is the realized outcome category (one-hot vector), which reveals the realized profit and is richer than scalar bandit feedback
Learner knows the number of outcomes m and the public value vector v, but not action sets, costs, type distribution or outcome laws
settings.definition_quote: At each round, a type $\theta$ is drawn independently from a fixed distribution. Type $\theta$ has an action set $A_\theta$. Action $a$ has outcome law $p_{\theta,a}\in\Delta_m$ and cost $c_{\theta,a}\in\mathbb R$. For every $\theta$ and $f$, a selected response $a_\theta(f)\in\argmax_{a\in A_\theta}\{p_{\theta,a}\cdot f-c_{\theta,a}\}$ exists, is fixed independently of the learner's history ... The principal's expected one-period utility is $u(f)=P(f)\cdot(v-f)$ ... $\mathfrak R_T=T\sup_{f\in[0,1]^m}u(f)-\mathbb E[\sum_{t=1}^T u(f_t)]$.

conditions: m_out >= 2 fixed; constant C_m depends only on m_out
selected best response fixed independently of history (Assumption 1)
tuning: B_m a sufficiently large dimension-only constant

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: For every fixed $m\ge2$, there exists a finite constant $B_m$, depending only on $m$, such that, for every $T\ge2$ and $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, Algorithms~\ref{alg:simulator}-\ref{alg:master} with confidence $\delta=T^{-2}$ use only $m$, $v$, $T$, and $\varepsilon$ and satisfy, on every instance in $\mathcal I_m$, \[\mathfrak R_T\le C_m\big(T\varepsilon+L_T\sqrt{TK_\varepsilon}+K_\varepsilon\big),\] where $K_\varepsilon\le(1+3\sqrt{m-1}/\varepsilon)^{m-1}$ and $L_T=1+\log^3(16K_\varepsilon T^3)$.

results.notes: Regret is through expected utility u(f), so pseudo_regret. Feedback mapped to partial_monitoring since algorithm uses outcome category (richer than scalar bandit). Compute: grid polynomial in T for fixed m, exponential in m.

conditions: m_out >= 2 fixed; hidden constant depends on m_out
selected best response fixed independently of history (Assumption 1)
tuning: eps ~ T^{-1/(m+1)} up to log factors

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: Consequently, $\varepsilon\asymp T^{-1/(m+1)}$ up to logarithmic factors gives $\mathfrak R_T\le\widetilde O_m(T^{m/(m+1)})$.

results.notes: Optimized consequence of the fixed-scale bound.

conditions: m_out >= 2 fixed; constant c_m depends on m_out
hard instances: single type, finite action set, public value (1,...,1,0), nonnegative costs bounded by one, common deterministic action-priority tie-breaking
alternatives differ from baseline only in one action cost

source.label: thm:lower
source.quote: For every fixed $m\ge2$, there is $c_m>0$ such that every adaptive outcome-feedback policy and every $T\ge1$ incur $\mathfrak R_T\ge c_mT^{m/(m+1)}$ on some finite-action, single-type instance in $\mathcal I_m$.

results.notes: Combined with Theorem 2 gives minimax regret tilde-Theta_m(T^{m/(m+1)}).
